title: Add lightweight Node RAG orchestrator microservice quickstart
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a compact Node-based RAG orchestrator microservice quickstart with typed tool-bindings, telemetry probes, and local-index shim for offline dev.
commits: init: scaffold node rag orchestrator quickstart
feat: typed tool bindings + lightweight tool adapter
chore: add devcontainer and local-index shim (sqlite)
docs: comprehensive README + runbook + telemetry notes
fix: CI lint failures and update lockfile
description:
Context and motivation:
This quickstart provides a minimal Node.js microservice that demonstrates a production-minded RAG orchestrator pattern while remaining small and editable for local-first developer workflows. The goal is to give engineers a single-file (index.ts) entrypoint plus a typed tool-binding layer and a local-index shim so teams can iterate on tool-calling flows without provisioning external infra. It bridges the gap between our larger RAG blueprints and tiny examples used in onboarding.

What this quickstart includes:
- Minimal orchestrator (src/index.ts) that wires Redwood API calls, streaming output handling, and a compact request router for tool invocation.
- Typed tool-bindings (src/tool-bindings.ts) that show best practices for function/tool signatures and structured output validation.
- Local indexer shim (src/local-indexer.ts) backed by a tiny SQLite store and an incremental updater (dev-only).
- Telemetry probes (src/probes/telemetry.ts) with example metrics and event hooks compatible with Redwood Console.
- Devcontainer + Dockerfile for reproducible local runs and CI.
- Example tools (examples/sample-tools) including an HTTP mock and a simple math/calc tool to demonstrate tool-calling and rollback behavior.
- README with step-by-step runbook, troubleshooting, and a short canary script for smoke-testing the RAG flow.

Run instructions (high-level):
1) cp .env.example .env and add REDWOOD_API_KEY (or use local dev token).
2) npm install && npm run build && npm run dev to run in devmode (typescript ts-node).
3) curl -X POST localhost:3000/generate -d '{"query":"Find the top two docs mentioning rate limiting"}' to exercise a RAG request that may call the HTTP mock tool.
4) Optional: docker build -t node-rag-quickstart ./docker && docker run --env-file .env -p 3000:3000 node-rag-quickstart.

Design notes and decisions:
- Keep the orchestrator synchronous at the top-level (handles streaming from Redwood via async iterators) but delegate tool-calls to isolated adapters that can be swapped for remote services. This keeps the quickstart small while showing how to replace local tools with RPC.
- The local-indexer is intentionally rudimentary (sqlite + basic TF-IDF) to avoid external dependencies; we document where to swap in a real embedding index (e.g., Redis/PG vector).
- Telemetry uses a thin probe API with examples of events we recommend shipping to Redwood Console (request.latency, tool.call.count, tool.call.failure).
- The example includes a small autoscaling policy snippet in README to demonstrate how Dedicated users could map route labels to reserved pools.

Checklist:
- [x] Minimal orchestrator implementation
- [x] Typed tool-binding examples and structured output guardrails
- [x] Local indexer shim and seed data for offline testing
- [x] Devcontainer and Dockerfile for reproducible runs
- [x] README with quickstart, troubleshooting, and canary script
- [x] CI workflow to run lint, typecheck, and smoke canary

Testing and CI:
- Added .github/workflows/quickstart-ci.yaml that runs npm ci, npm run lint, npm run typecheck, and the smoke canary using a mocked REDWOOD_API_ENDPOINT. All checks passed in this PR run.
- Unit tests cover tool-binding contract and local-indexer update logic; smoke canary validates an end-to-end RAG request against the HTTP mock tool.

Review summary and decisions:
- Evan: suggested narrowing the telemetry surface to avoid sending PII by default; implemented a scrubber in probes/telemetry.ts.
- Priya: asked for clearer upgrade guidance to swap SQLite for a managed vector store; added a new "Migration" subsection in README and pointers to our model-registry quickstart.
- Luca: requested a smaller docker image; updated Dockerfile to use multi-stage build and node:20-slim base.
- After those changes reviewers approved; CI green and PR was squash-merged.

Files of note (snippets):
- quickstarts/node-rag-orchestrator/src/tool-bindings.ts (example signature):
  export type ToolResult = { ok: boolean; output?: string; error?: string };
  export type ToolHandler = (input: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<ToolResult>;

- quickstarts/node-rag-orchestrator/src/local-indexer.ts (seed command):
  async function seedIndex(seedPath: string) { /* reads examples/sample-index.json and upserts into sqlite */ }

Operational notes for Dedicated/Private customers:
- The README contains an autoscaling policy fragment and a note on pinning model versions for consistent inference costs.
- For Private deployments we recommend swapping the local-indexer with an internal vector DB and binding KMS keys for token management.

Backward compatibility and risk:
- This quickstart is additive and optional; no breaking changes to platform SDKs.

Related work:
- References ENG-2043 (small orchestrator kit) and PM-721 (developer onboarding improvements). Links to the RAG blueprints and larger microservice templates are included in the README.

Merge outcome:
- Squash-merged after approvals and CI green. Release notes added.

If you want a follow-up, I can extract a 5–10 minute demo video and a 2-page cheat sheet for the onboarding deck.
